JUDGMENT

Plaintiff has filed the instant suit for declaration that he is the absolute owner of the suit property,
permanent injunction restraining defendants from interfering with his possession and enjoyment of the said property, alternatively if the court finds that plaintiff is not in possession of the suit property directing defendants to hand over the possession of the said property to him, means profit and cost.

O.S.No. 26589/2014 FACTS OF THE CASE:
2. Smt. Lakshmamma, the defendants mother is the elder sister of the plaintiff.
Defendants father Late.
Venkatswamy was having 13 guntas of land in Sy.No.63/2 of Chalaghatta Village, HAL Sanitary board, Varthur Hobli, Bangalore South Taluk.
He acquire the said property under the registered Will dated 15/06/1956 made by Sri.Muniswamappa.

After the death of Sri. Venkatswamy, the defendants father, the katha of the said property got mutated in the name of his widow Smt.
Lakshmamma.
She was suffering from Cancer.
As a brother plaintiff was providing financial assistance to his sister and brought up her children viz defentants.

Keeping in the mind the said fact Smt. Lakshmamma bequeathed two guntas of land in Sy.No.63/2 of Chalaghatta Village, which is more fully described in the plaint schedule and here in after refered to as suit property in favour of plaintiff by executing Will dated 21/09/2011.
She bequeathed the remaining land in Sy.No.63/2 in favour of her children Viz defendants.
Plaintiff contends that his sister Smt. Lakshmamma died on 04/07/2011.
After her death the Will made by her came into O.S.No. 26589/2014 force and he became the absolute owner of suit property.
As owner he is in possession and enjoyment of the said property.
Defendants the children of Smt. Lakshmamma started interfering with his possession of said property.
Therefore, he filed the instant suit.

On these and other grounds stated in the plaint,
plaintiff prays to decree the suit and to grant the relief as prayed for.

His sister 2nd defendant adopted the written statement of 1st defendant.

sentences.text: PW.2 in the cross-examination at page No.6 para No.5 has stated that Ex.P. 5 Will was made in the house of Lakshmamma, at that time Lakshmamma's son, the 1 st defendant , Srinivas and his wife were present.

As stated by PW.2 if the 1st defendant and his wife were present at the time of making the Will the 1st defendant would have given consent to make the said Will and he or/and his wife could have made signature on the Will.
PW.2 has not stated any reason for non-taking the signature of 1 st defendant or his O.S.No. 26589/2014 wife on Ex.P. 5 Will despite they were pesent at the time of making the wife.
20. PW.1 has stated that after making of Will, Lakshmamma whose health condition was very critical came to his house and handedover the Will to him.

As stated by P.W.2 if the son of Lakshmamma was present at the time of making Ex.P. 5 Will and he gave consent for making Will there was no necessity for Lakshmamma whose health condition was very critical to go to the house of plaintiff to handover the Will.
She could have sent the said Will through her son, the 1st defendant to handover it to the plaintiff .
21. Admittedly, immediately after the death of Lakshmamma plaintiff not acted upon on Ex.P. 5 Will.
Lakshmamma died on 4.11.2011.
plaintiff has filed the instant suit on 21.11.2011 ie., 3 years of making of the alleged Will.
For 3 years, Ex.P. 5 Will has not seen the light of the day.

As contended by plaintiff in view of financial assistance provided by him to his sister and her children, if Lakshmamma would have made Ex.P. 5 Will and as stated by Pw.2 if the 1st defendant, would have present and given consent to the Will, immediately after the death of O.S.No. 26589/2014 Lakshmamma, plaintiff could have produced the said Will before Revenue authorities to effect mutation.

The fact that Ex.P. 5 Will has not seen the light of the day for 3 years and no step was taken by the plaintiff to enter his name in the BBMP records of the suit property on the basis of Will would create suspicion to believe Ex.P. 5 Will.
22.
A perusal of Ex.P. 5 Will would show that it was made on two plain papers.
Usually at the end of the Will certificate will be made to the effect that the testator made the Will out of his free will and volition in the presence of witnesses.
But, in Ex.P. 5 Will the above recitals were typed in the first page.
After the said certificate in bracket the schedule is stated and after the schedule, it is also stated the testator's children can divide the remaining extent of land in Sy.No. 63/2.
On careful perusal of page No.2 of Ex.P5 Will would show that some words of the Will were typed the thumb impression.
In Ex.P5 Will an advocate by name Devarajai.H has signed with certificate that he drafted the Will.

If an advocate having legal knowledge drafted a Will and at the time of taking signature he was of an opinion that in addition to signature of the testator it is better to take O.S.No.
26589/2014 his/her thumb impression , he will take thumb impression on all the pages of the Will.
A perusal of Ex.P. 5 Will would show that the thumb impression of Lakshmamma is there only on page No.2 and there is no thumb impression on page No.1.
This would create suspicion to believe Ex.P5 Will and would support the contention of the defendants that by using blank signed papers Will was created.

sentences.text: In the cross-examination at page No.9 PW.2 has stated that on 21.09.2011 after finishing his office work, he came to his residence at about 5.30pm; his mother-in-law called and informed him to go to the house of Lakshmamma, accordingly, he went to the house of Lakshmamma.

He stated that when he reached the house of Lakshmamma,
Lakshmamma, her son, the first defendant Srinivasa, his O.S.No. 26589/2014 wife, witness Chandra Reddy and advocate were present.
Thus from the facts stated by PW.2 would show that on 21.09.2011 Lakshmamma or her children did not call him to come to their house to become witness to the Will.

The statement of Pw.2 that he went to the house of Lakshmamma as per the instructions given by his mother-in-law would show that the family members and plaintiff took active part in preparation of the Will.
24. PW.2 has stated that at the time of making Ex.P.5 will 1st defendant was pesent.
1st defendant was examined as DW.1.
In his cross-examination, no attempt was made to elicit that at the time of making the Will, he was present and he gave consent for making the Will.
P.W.1 in the cross-examination at page No.10 has stated that after the death of Lakshmamma he orally informed her children viz., defendants about Ex.P. 5 Will.

As stated by PW.2 if Ex.P. 5 Will would have been made in the presence of 1st defendant and his wife, there was no necessity for the plaintiff to inform about the said Will to O.S.No. 26589/2014 defendants after the death of Lakshmamma.

Therefore,
the statement of PW.1 that after the death of Lakshmamma he informed her children about Ex.P. 5 Will would give an indication that during the life time of Lakshmamma her children had no knowledge about the said Will.
25. Admittedly, the land in Sy.No. 63/2 measuring 13 guntas was the self-acquired property of defendant's father late Venkataswamy.
During his life time, 4 guntas of land was acquired by Government to lay pipelines.
Admittedly, Venkataswamy died intestate.
After his death, his widow and children viz., defendants would succeed to the said 9 guntas of land.
Therefore, Lakshmamma was not the absolute owner of said 9 guntas of land.

Admittedly, after the death of Venkataswamy,
there was no partition between his legal heirs viz Lakshmamma and defendants.

Therefore,
Lakshmamma had no right to alienate or bequeath a definite portion of property in the said 9 guntas of land.
O.S.No. 26589/2014 She can alienate or bequeath only her undivided interest in the said 9 guntas of land.
26. In Ex.P. 5 Will it is stated that the land in Sy.No. 63/2 is measuring 13 guntas .

A perusal of Ex.D. 3 award would show that in the year 1972 Government has acquired 4 guntas of land in Sy.No.
63/2.
As contended by plaintiff if Lakshmamma would have made Ex.P. 5 Will she could have stated that after acquisition of 4 guntas in Sy.No. 63/2, only 9 guntas of land is remaining.
In Ex.P. 5 Will it is stated that out of 13 guntas of land, Will was made in respect of 2 guntas of land.

A perusal of sketch enclosed to Ex.D. 3 LAC award would show that eastern portion of land measuring 4 guntas was acquired by Government for laying water pipes.

If Lakshmamma out of her free will and volition, would have made Ex.P5 O.S.No.

This is also one of the suspicious circumstance surrounding Ex.P. 5 Will.
28.
The Ld. Counsel for the defendants placed reliance on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Bharpur Singh & Ors Vs Shamsher Singh reported in 2009 SC 1766.

sentences.text: In the said case, it is stated that if the Will is surrounded by suspicious circumstances, the propounder/legatee has to give reasonable explanation to remove such suspicious circumstances.
29. In the instant case, according to the plaintiff the main reason for making a Will is the financial assistance and help provided by him to his sister Lakshmamma and her children.
Absolutely there is zero O.S.No. 26589/2014 evidence to prove that plaintiff provided financial assistance to his sister Lakshmamma and her children.
30. From the facts stated by PW.2, the son-in-law of plaintiff would show that during the life time of Lakshmamma he was not in touch with her.
Therefore, Lakshmamma requesting PW.2 to become a witness of her Will appears to be not true.
31. PW.2 has stated that the son of Lakshmamma viz 1st defendant and his wife were pesent at the time of making the Will.
No explanation was given why their signatures were not taken on the Will.
32. Plaintiff has not examined Advocate who alleged to have drafted the Will.
Another witness of will by name Chandrappa Reddy is the relative of plaintiff's wife.
Plaintiff has not examined him .
PW.2 has stated that he was not present when the Will was made, Lakshmamma did not call him to her house to become the witness of the Will and he do not know the name of Advocate who prepared Will.
From this it is clear that O.S.No. 26589/2014 PW.2 is not having complete knowledge regarding making of Will.
33. Having regard to the medical evidence available on record, the statement of PW.2 that at the time of making Ex.P5 Will, Lakshmamma was hale and healthy does not inspire confidence in the court.

34. In view of my aforesaid findings I hold that a bare perusal of Ex.P. 5 Will which was made on two plain thin papers having certificate at the first page which normally would be there at the end and typing of some of the recitals on the thumb impression of Lakshmamma would create serious suspicion to believe Ex.P. 5 Will and would support the contention of the defendants that it was created by using signatures of Lakshmamma on blank papers.
35. The fact that Ex.P. 5 Will has not seen the light of the day for 3 years after the death of Lakshmamma would also create suspicion to believe the Will.

In view of my aforesaid findings, I hold that plaintiff failed to prove O.S.No. 26589/2014 that Lakshmamma made Ex.P. 5 Will out of her free will and volition when she was in a sound disposed state of mind.
In view of the above, I answer Issue No.1 in the Negative.

sentences.text: ISSUE No.2:- Plaintiff has not stated after the death of Lakshmamma when he took the possession of suit property .
From the facts stated by DW.1 would show that after the death of Lakshmamma, he and his sister, the 2nd defendant are in joint possession of the entire 9 guntas of land in Sy.No. 63/2.
Thus, plaintiff failed to prove his possession over the suit property .
In view of plaintiff is not certain about his possession over the suit property he alternatively sought the relief of possession.
In view of the above, I hold that plaintiff fails to prove his possession over the suit property as on the date of suit .
Accordingly I answer Issue No.2 in the Negative.
In view of my findings on Issue No.2 in the Negative, Issue No.3 is to be answered in the Negative.
Accordingly it is answered in the Negative.
38. ISSUE NO.4:-
In view of my reasons and findings on Issue No.1 to 4, plaintiff is not entitled for the relief of declaration , injunction or possession.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.4 in the Negative.
39. ISSUE NO.5:-

In view of my reasons and findings on above Issues I pass the following:
ORDER Plaintiff's suit is dismissed.
No order as to cost.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Plaintiff has filed the instant suit for declaration that he is the absolute owner of the suit property,
permanent injunction restraining defendants from interfering with his possession and enjoyment of the said property, alternatively if the court finds that plaintiff is not in possession of the suit property directing defendants to hand over the possession of the said property to him, means profit and cost.
He acquire the said property under the registered Will dated 15/06/1956 made by Sri.Muniswamappa.
After the death of Sri. Venkatswamy, the defendants father, the katha of the said property got mutated in the name of his widow Smt.
Lakshmamma.
She was suffering from Cancer.
As a brother plaintiff was providing financial assistance to his sister and brought up her children viz defentants.
She bequeathed the remaining land in Sy.No.63/2 in favour of her children Viz defendants.
Plaintiff contends that his sister Smt. Lakshmamma died on 04/07/2011.
After her death the Will made by her came into O.S.No. 26589/2014 force and he became the absolute owner of suit property.
As owner he is in possession and enjoyment of the said property.
Defendants the children of Smt. Lakshmamma started interfering with his possession of said property.
Therefore, he filed the instant suit.
3. 1st defendant resisted the suit by filing the written statement.
They contend that their mother Smt. Lakshmamma was suffering from Cancer stage 4.
They contend that after the death of their father Sri. Venkataswamy they and their mother Smt. Lakshmamma were in joint possession and enjoyment of 9 guntas of land in Sy.No.63/2.
After the death of their mother Smt. Lakshmamma they are in joint possession of the said 9 guntas of land.
They contend that the said 9 guntas of land situate within the limits of BBMP and thus it become non agricultural land.
They contend that their mother Smt. Lakshamamma not given the suit property to plaintiff by making will.
Plaintiff was never in possession of the suit property.
Therefore, the question of they interfering with plaintiff's possession and enjoyment of suit property would not arise.
They contend that plaintiff has no manner of any right, title,
interest or possession over the suit property.
Therefor, he has no locus standi to file the instant suit.
There is no cause of O.S.No. 26589/2014 action for the suit.
The cause of action one alleged in the plaint is false and imaginary.
The plaintiff contends that as a brother he provided financial assistance to his elder sister Smt.
Lakshmamma and brought up her children.
Taken into consideration the said fact his sister Smt. Lakshmamma bequeathed suit property in his favour by making Will dated 21/09/2011.
Defendants stoutly denied the execution of the Will.
They contend that after the death of their mother Smt. Lakshmamma they and their Aunt filed a suit for partition claiming share in the joint family property of their mother Smt. Lakshmamma.
Therefore, plaintiff filed the instant suit by creating the Will dated 21/09/2011.
